name: gauntlgrym
lore:
/toril/faerun/underdark/gauntlgrym
[category: city]

Greetings, seeker of knowledge. I am a Lorekeeper of Candlekeep, and within these grand halls of learning, few tales stir the soul quite like the saga of Gauntlgrym. Pull up a chair, and let us delve into the deep history of the most legendary dwarven stronghold in the North.

Gauntlgrym is a subterranean marvel situated in the Upper Underdark, specifically deep beneath the Crags, a mountain range nestled along the Sword Coast North in Northwest Faerûn. The city is a masterpiece of ancient engineering, boasting cavernous halls, intricately carved pillars, and sprawling, gem-rich mines. The beating heart of the settlement is the legendary Great Forge. This massive smithy is powered by a structure known as the Burning Heart, which contains a fiery pit holding Maegera the Dawn Titan, a slumbering primordial of fire. It is said that the heat harnessed from Maegera allows the dwarves to forge weapons and armor that are virtually peerless in all of Toril.

Constructed during the zenith of the dwarven empire of Delzoun, Gauntlgrym was a testament to unprecedented cooperation. The dwarves did not build it alone; ancient pacts were struck with the human arcanists of Illusk and the elves of Iliyanbruen to weave the arcane and natural wards necessary to safely bind the primordial Maegera. For a golden age, Gauntlgrym stood as a beacon of civilization and unparalleled craftsmanship. However, like many great empires, it was destined to fall. Successive invasions by hordes of orcs, and later the insidious mind flayers, broke the city's defenses. Gauntlgrym was eventually abandoned, its halls sealed and slipping into the realm of myth for centuries.

For ages, countless adventurers sought the lost city, but it remained hidden until its rediscovery in the late 15th century DR. The city's reawakening was fraught with tragedy. In the year 1451 DR, machinations involving the Thayan lich Valindra Shadowmantle, alongside mercenaries such as the drow Jarlaxle, disturbed the slumbering primordial. This catastrophic event triggered the violent eruption of Mount Hotenow, devastating the surface city of Neverwinter located far above. 

During the era of the Second Sundering, the fabled halls were claimed by the dark elves of Menzoberranzan. In 1484 DR, under the command of Matron Mother Zeerith, House Xorlarrin conquered the ruins, renaming the settlement Q'Xorlarrin. They sought to use the city's formidable forges and strategic position to assert dominance over the Underdark. For a brief period, it seemed the legacy of Delzoun was entirely eclipsed by the shadow of the Spider Queen.

Yet, the spirit of the dwarves is as unyielding as mithral. In 1486 DR, the reincarnated King Bruenor Battlehammer rallied a grand host and secured the upper reaches of the city. Descending into the depths, Bruenor's forces drove House Xorlarrin out, forcing them to retreat to Menzoberranzan in disgrace. Bruenor was rightfully crowned King of Gauntlgrym, and he immediately set to the task of clearing the remaining halls for resettlement. 

Since its reclamation, the city has once again become a thriving bastion of dwarven power and a crucial defensive stronghold against the horrors of the deep. When the calamitous Rage of Demons brought abyssal lords to the Underdark, King Bruenor and the forces of Gauntlgrym served as a vital staging ground, calling upon brave adventurers to combat the demonic incursion. Today, the hammers ring out once more in the Great Forge, singing a song of dwarven resilience powered by the eternal heat of the Dawn Titan.
